draft.title: From making goods to providing services
card: Goods are things you can touch, such as wheat, wool and cars. Services are things people do for others, such as teaching, nursing and cutting hair.
A long time ago, most Australians worked in farming, mining or factories. These jobs produce goods.
Today most Australians work in services, such as health care, education, retail and professional work like accounting and law.
Goods are still made and grown in Australia. The change is that a much larger share of jobs is now in services.
draft.remember: Work has shifted from mostly making goods to mostly providing services.

a.q: Which job is an example of a service?
opts: A nurse caring for patients at a hospital
A farmer growing wheat in the Mallee
A worker building cars in a factory
A miner digging iron ore from the ground
a.why: A nurse does something for other people, so the job is a service. The other three jobs produce things you can touch, which are goods.
a.clue: Which job is about doing something for someone?

b.q: Mia says that Australia now makes no goods because most people work in services. What is wrong with her claim?
opts: Goods are still made, but most jobs are now in services
Most Australians still work in farming and factories
Services are now made by machines, not by people
Australia now has fewer jobs than it did before
b.why: The card says goods are still grown and made in Australia. What has changed is the share of jobs, which is now mostly in services. Saying most jobs are in services does not mean no goods are made.
b.clue: Most jobs in services is not the same as no goods at all.

a.best: A nurse caring for patients at a hospital

b.best: Goods are still made, but most jobs are now in services

problems.detail: The clue ('Most jobs in services is not the same as no goods at all') nearly restates the right option, so a student can match it without understanding the idea.
